<USER_REQUEST>
ROLE
You are a senior Python full-stack developer and acoustics-aware engineer. Build a complete, working, visually impressive, multi-page interactive website called "UrbanSound 3D: Noise Pollution Propagation Simulator" for a 3rd-semester engineering project titled "Simulation Framework for Noise Pollution Propagation Analysis in Urban Areas". Use PYTHON TOOLS for the entire project.

GOAL
A visitor with no technical background should open the site, understand what noise pollution propagation is, then run a realistic simulation, see results in 3D maps and graphs, and test fixes (sound barriers, traffic reduction) before/after. It must feel like a real planning tool: interactive, explanatory, and polished.

TECH STACK (Python only)
- Streamlit multipage app (pages/ folder) with custom CSS and st.components.v1.html for scroll-reveal animations
- Plotly (go.Mesh3d, go.Surface, go.Heatmap, go.Scatter3d, line/bar/histogram charts) for ALL 3D and 2D visualizations
- NumPy (vectorized calculations), Pandas, Shapely + GeoPandas (building geometry and obstruction), OSMnx (optional real city data; app must also work fully OFFLINE with synthetic cities), Matplotlib only if needed for exports
- Pillow/SVG/CSS-generated graphics for the landing page (generate visuals in code; do not depend on external image URLs)
- requirements.txt, README.md with setup + run steps (pip install -r requirements.txt; streamlit run Home.py)

SITE STRUCTURE (4 pages, shared dark modern theme, sidebar navigation)
1) Home.py: animated scroll-story landing page (details below)
2) pages/1_Simulator.py: interactive setup and live 3D simulation
3) pages/2_Results_and_Compare.py: analysis, compliance, before/after scenarios, day/night, export
4) pages/3_Methodology.py: the physics, formulas, assumptions, limitations, references

PAGE 1: HOME (creative, scroll-driven storytelling)
Use a hero section, then reveal sections as the user scrolls (CSS animations / IntersectionObserver inside an HTML component: fade-in, slide
<truncated 6359 bytes>
octave bands, static sources, no weather turbulence, no multiple reflections), validation notes, future scope (moving traffic, ML surrogate, sensor data), and a references list (ISO 9613-2:2024; CPCB noise rules; WHO environmental noise guidelines).

CODE STRUCTURE
Home.py, pages/1_Simulator.py, pages/2_Results_and_Compare.py, pages/3_Methodology.py, core/propagation.py, core/sources.py, core/geometry.py (cities, buildings, barriers), core/visualization.py (all Plotly figures), core/standards.py (CPCB/WHO limits), core/utils.py, assets/style.css, tests/test_propagation.py, requirements.txt, README.md.

QUALITY AND USABILITY
- Consistent professional dark theme, readable fonts, color-blind-friendly alternate palette toggle
- Tooltips/help text on every input in plain English
- Friendly error handling and input validation; offline fallback; no crashes on empty source list
- Use st.session_state so settings persist between pages
- Modular, commented code with docstrings explaining every formula
- Unit tests: 6 dB drop per doubling of distance, energy summation (60+60 about 63 dB), barrier reduces the level behind it, no negative attenuation
- Add a visible disclaimer: this is an academic simplified model, not a certified regulatory tool

DELIVERY ORDER
1) Show the folder structure. 2) Build core/ (propagation, geometry, standards) with tests. 3) Build visualization functions. 4) Build the Simulator page. 5) Build Results and Methodology pages. 6) Build the Home landing page with scroll animations. 7) Give exact run instructions. After each stage, make sure the app runs without errors before moving on.
